nodes.label: ProfilePolish
nodes.rationale: A free, private LinkedIn and resume coach for college students. Exists because commercial AI LinkedIn tools cost Rs 500-2,000/month and keep profiles on their servers; students need neither the cost nor the server-side storage.

nodes.label: Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)
nodes.rationale: The browser talks to the AI provider directly with the student's own free-tier key. Chosen because if the server never holds the key or the prompt, there is nothing on the server that can leak; it also keeps hosting cost at zero since inference is billed to the student's free quota.

nodes.label: Shared-Key Proxy (/api/generate)
nodes.rationale: A serverless route that forwards one prompt to Gemini using the host's own key, streams the reply, sets Cache-Control: no-store and stores nothing. It is the single deliberate exception to the client-side-only rule, so a student with no key of their own is not blocked in the first two minutes.

nodes.label: Privacy Model Table
nodes.rationale: Per-datum table of where each item lives, for how long, and whether it ever reaches the server. Published in the README so the privacy promise is auditable rather than asserted; any PR that adds a network call must keep it true.

nodes.label: Zero-Cost Hosting Constraint
nodes.rationale: Vercel Hobby plus optional free-tier keys, no card anywhere. Deliberate, so any student group or college can fork and run their own instance without a budget or an approval process.

nodes.label: LinkedIn PDF Export Ingestion
nodes.rationale: LinkedIn offers no API for reading profiles and scraping is out, so the supported path is the Save to PDF export the student already owns. The parser is heuristic on purpose: the AI always receives the full extracted text, so a mis-detected section does not degrade the suggestions.

nodes.label: Onboarding Page
nodes.rationale: Drag-drop the LinkedIn PDF, paste text, or skip entirely. Skipping is allowed so the under-two-minutes constraint holds even for a student without an export to hand.

nodes.label: Profile Optimizer
nodes.rationale: Runs 13 rule-based completeness checks with no AI call first, then an optional AI review. The rule pass exists so a student with no key still gets useful output immediately.

nodes.label: Message Writer
nodes.rationale: Six outreach message types with three variants each (short / warm / direct) plus a when-to-send tip. Cited in the README as the simplest full page to copy when adding a new feature.

nodes.label: Resume ATS Check
nodes.rationale: 13 zero-AI rule checks (contact info, headings, length, action verbs, metrics, cliches, table artefacts, JD keyword match) before any model call, then an optional AI review. Same rationale as the profile gap check: useful without a key, and cheap on free quota.

nodes.label: My Drafts
nodes.rationale: Saved drafts with a visible 48-hour countdown and Markdown export. The countdown is shown rather than hidden because expiry is a privacy feature, and export is the escape hatch for anything worth keeping.

nodes.label: Settings Page
nodes.rationale: Per-provider key instructions, model dropdown, session-only keys by default with opt-in remember-on-this-device, and one-click clear-all. Defaults are tuned for a shared college lab computer rather than a personal laptop.

nodes.label: Trending Feed (/api/trending)
nodes.rationale: Server route aggregating Google Trends (India) RSS, Hacker News and Dev.to, cached hourly. It is one of only two server routes, which is why the app cannot be a purely static site.

nodes.label: Shared-Key Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: Per-device, per-IP and global daily counters keep the host's free Gemini quota from being drained by one user. Upstash Redis is optional; without it counters are in-memory per serverless instance and reset on cold start, which is accepted as best-effort for a small pilot.

nodes.label: Model Catalog and Defaults
nodes.rationale: Curated defaults per provider (Gemini and Groq free, OpenAI and Anthropic paid) plus a Load models from provider button. The live-list button exists because model ids churn every few months and a hardcoded dropdown goes stale.

nodes.label: Honest Limitations List
nodes.rationale: No LinkedIn API, free-tier quotas, best-effort shared-key limits, clearable browser storage, and fallible AI output are stated up front. Publishing the failure modes is the same commitment as the do-not-oversell invariant applied to the docs.

nodes.label: Fork-and-Own Design
nodes.rationale: MIT licensed and structured so a fork takes five minutes: rename in config.ts, recolour via CSS variables in globals.css, deploy. Contributing back is explicitly optional, so a college can run its own instance without asking permission.

nodes.label: Workshop Slide Deck and Speaker Script
nodes.rationale: 21-slide MBA-edition deck plus script for running a LinkedIn session. The recommended demo is live profile review rather than slides, because two minutes of real output convinces where a slide does not.
nodes.norm_label: workshop slide deck and speaker script

nodes.label: Tech Stack and Folder Structure
nodes.rationale: Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, Tailwind 4, Dexie/IndexedDB, pdf.js, mammoth, and four official provider SDKs each lazy-loaded only when chosen so a Gemini user never downloads the other three bundles.

nodes.label: Three Founding Constraints
nodes.rationale: Must cost the host Rs 0; student data must never reach the server; a student must be usable in under two minutes on a shared lab computer without an account. Stated as the root from which the whole design follows: a change that breaks one is the wrong change however good the feature.

nodes.label: Ten Hard Invariants
nodes.rationale: A numbered, never-break table so reviewers can cite a breakage by number rather than argue taste. Each row pairs the rule with its why, making the table usable by both humans and the automated Claude PR reviewer.

nodes.label: Invariant 1: BYOK Calls Go Browser to Provider Directly
nodes.rationale: A student's API key must never be sent to the server, logged, or put in a URL. Stated why: if the server never holds it, it cannot leak it.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 1: byok calls go browser to provider directly

nodes.label: Invariant 2: Student Content Stays Client-Side
nodes.rationale: Profile text, resume text and drafts live in IndexedDB or component state; the only exception is the shared-key proxy, which forwards one prompt to Gemini and stores nothing. This is the product's promise, published in the README and in-app.

nodes.label: Invariant 3: No Server-Side Database, Accounts or Auth
nodes.rationale: Holding resumes and keys server-side without real auth is a liability, and adding auth breaks the under-two-minutes-no-account constraint. The trade-off is resolved by having neither.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 3: no server-side database, accounts or auth

nodes.label: Invariant 4: Everything in the Browser Has a TTL
nodes.rationale: Drafts and the parsed profile expire after DRAFT_TTL_MS (48 hours) and are purged on app load, because the app is used on shared computers.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 4: everything in the browser has a ttl

nodes.label: Invariant 5: Keys Default to sessionStorage
nodes.rationale: localStorage is opt-in behind a Remember on this device toggle with a shared-computer warning, because the target device is a lab machine used by many students.

nodes.label: Invariant 6: No Direct DOM Manipulation
nodes.rationale: UI is driven through React state; the single allowed exception is a detached anchor element for file downloads in drafts/page.tsx. React owns the DOM, and mutating it underneath causes bugs that only appear in production builds.

nodes.label: Invariant 7: Prompts Must Forbid Invention
nodes.rationale: Every prompt tells the model not to invent achievements, numbers, companies or skills and to mark gaps as [add number], because students paste the output into real applications.

nodes.label: Invariant 8: No Secret in Client Code or Commits
nodes.rationale: Server secrets live only in Vercel env vars and .env* is git-ignored. Called out as obvious but easy to slip, which is why the checklist includes a grep for provider key prefixes in the diff.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 8: no secret in client code or commits

nodes.label: Invariant 9: No Analytics Capturing Page Content or Input
nodes.rationale: Any analytics that reads page content or user input would silently break the privacy promise the host is told to make to students.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 9: no analytics capturing page content or input

nodes.label: Invariant 10: Don't Oversell
nodes.rationale: Copy describes what the app does (polish, draft, check) and never promises replies, interviews or jobs. The app was renamed from CareerLift to ProfilePolish for exactly this reason.

nodes.label: Task-to-File Map (CLAUDE.md)
nodes.rationale: A short task-to-file table (prompts.ts, config.ts, client.ts, ats.ts, profile-gaps.ts, trending.ts, profile-parser.ts, db.ts, keys.ts, ratelimit.ts, ui.tsx) so an assistant can find the right file without reading the full tree.

nodes.label: Code Conventions
nodes.rationale: TypeScript strict with no any, Server Components by default, browser-only reads gated behind useIsClient() after hydration, no synchronous setState inside useEffect, lazily loaded provider SDKs, comments that explain why not what, and copy written for a 19-year-old in a hurry.

nodes.label: Pre-Merge Verification Checklist
nodes.rationale: Seven steps: build and checks, explicit invariant greps on src/lib/ai, keys.ts, db.ts and API routes, a secret-prefix grep on the diff, real browser exercise, the no-key path, privacy-claim accuracy, and docs updates. Results must be reported honestly rather than merged around.

nodes.label: Browser Verification Requirement
nodes.rationale: A page that compiles is not a page that works. Several historical bugs (a stuck loading spinner, a mis-parsed PDF section, an error visible only after clicking Generate) passed both tsc and eslint, so the changed path must be exercised end to end in a real browser.

nodes.label: PR Review Priority Order
nodes.rationale: Ranked: broken invariant (cite the number), leaked secret or student data, broken free-to-host constraint, build and function, honest student-readable copy, then everything else as suggestion. Explicitly forbids approving on green CI alone, since CI only checks types, lint and build.

nodes.label: Optional Automated Claude Review
nodes.rationale: Off by default and gated on an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY repository secret, so forks and contributors are never blocked and nobody spends the key owner's paid API credit without opting in.

nodes.label: Branch-and-PR Workflow
nodes.rationale: Every change goes on a feat/fix/docs/chore branch with a PR; never commit to main because main auto-deploys to production. Branches are never deleted without the owner asking.

nodes.label: Contributor Ground Rules
nodes.rationale: A five-point plain-language restatement of the invariants (zero cost, privacy is the product, no direct DOM manipulation, honest prompts, don't oversell), pointing at CLAUDE.md as the source of truth so contributors read the rules before a rewrite is needed.

nodes.label: Adding an AI Provider
nodes.rationale: Three steps: a providers/<name>.ts exporting StreamFn and ListModelsFn using the vendor SDK with browser access enabled, registration in client.ts under loaders and modelListers, and an entry in PROVIDERS in config.ts with a curated model list and key URL. Browser access is required because BYOK calls must not pass through the server.

nodes.label: Good First Contributions
nodes.rationale: New prompts, more ATS rules, more trending sources, better PDF parsing and UI translations are suggested first because they are pure functions or single-file changes that cannot break an invariant.

nodes.label: Branching Policy (CONTRIBUTING)
nodes.rationale: Work on a feat/fix/docs branch and open a PR against main; main deploys automatically, so a direct commit is a direct production deploy.

nodes.label: Private Security Advisory Reporting
nodes.rationale: Security issues go to a private GitHub security advisory rather than a public issue, so a disclosed weakness in the key-handling path is not broadcast before it is fixed.

nodes.label: What the Server Sees
nodes.rationale: With a student's own key the server sees nothing beyond static files and the trending feed. Written as what a host can truthfully tell students, so the claim is bounded by what the architecture actually guarantees.

nodes.label: Shared-Key Data Handling Disclosure
nodes.rationale: The prompt passes through /api/generate once, is forwarded to Google Gemini, and is streamed back with Cache-Control: no-store, never written to logs and never stored. Vercel's own request logs hold URL, status and timing but not request bodies, and that distinction is stated rather than glossed.

nodes.label: Anonymous Device Id and IP Counting
nodes.rationale: A random per-browser UUID plus the requester IP are used solely to count requests against the shared key's daily limits; with Upstash the counters live in Redis and expire after about 26 hours. The id is anonymous and header-only so fair rate limiting does not require identifying the student.
nodes.norm_label: anonymous device id and ip counting

nodes.label: What the Browser Stores
nodes.rationale: Defers to the README privacy table rather than duplicating it, noting the 48-hour TTL enforced on app load and the Clear all my data button.

nodes.label: Host Prohibitions
nodes.rationale: Three things a host must not do: add analytics that capture page content or inputs, log request bodies in /api/generate, or move keys and drafts to a server without adding real authentication first. Each maps to a specific invariant that would otherwise be broken silently by a well-meaning operational change.

nodes.label: CI check Job
nodes.rationale: Runs on push to main and every pull request: checkout, setup-node pinned from .nvmrc with npm cache, npm ci, tsc --noEmit, lint, build. Deliberately limited to types, lint and build, which is why the docs insist green CI is not evidence a change works.

nodes.label: Claude review Job
nodes.rationale: Runs anthropics/claude-code-action on PR opened and synchronize with a prompt that walks the CLAUDE.md pre-merge checklist and review priority order, flags broken invariants by number, and is instructed not to approve or merge and to say plainly what it could not verify.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Gate Step
nodes.rationale: A shell step writes enabled=true/false to GITHUB_OUTPUT depending on whether the secret exists, and every later step is conditioned on it, so the job skips cleanly on forks instead of failing and never spends credit that was not opted into.

nodes.label: Pull Request Checklist Template
nodes.rationale: Six boxes condensing the CLAUDE.md checklist: checks pass, no student data or keys reach the server (invariants 1-2), no paid service or always-on server, no secrets in the diff, opened it in a browser and used the thing changed, and docs updated.

nodes.label: Bug Report Issue Template
nodes.rationale: Asks for the AI provider and model and the browser and device, because the app runs almost entirely client-side against a user-chosen provider, so those two facts determine reproducibility more than any server state.

nodes.label: Feature Request Issue Template
nodes.rationale: Asks who the feature helps, with final-year students applying for placements given as the example, keeping proposals anchored to the target user rather than to generic product value.
